data.narrative:
Form Energy, a Series G climate and energy company founded by Mateo Jaramillo, Yet-Ming Chiang, and three others, has raised $750M to date. The valuation assessment draws on a universe of 9 same-sector peers (1 public, 8 private), including comparable-stage companies like Helion, Redwood Materials, and Electric Hydrogen, though a sufficiently tight peer cohort at identical stage and valuation tier could not be isolated.

Given the limited applicable triangulation methods, the Stage-Progression approach was employed as the primary quantitative lens. Using the $750M cumulative raised as a proxy baseline and applying a typical Series G step-up multiplier of 1.25x yields an implied valuation of $938M. This methodology assumes Form Energy's next-stage entry command a 25% premium—a conservative assumption for late-stage climate-tech given sector tailwinds, though one that cannot be independently validated without disclosed financial performance metrics.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $797M to $1.1B, centered on $938M. Material uncertainties remain unresolved: the absence of disclosed revenue, unit economics, or path to commercialization limits confidence in any estimate. Peer comparability is structural; the Climate & Energy sector spans heterogeneous technologies and commercialization timelines. A revised assessment incorporating operational milestones or narrower peer alignment would materially sharpen the range.
